title: Using Ecological Null Models to Assess the Potential for Marine Protected Area Networks to Protect Biodiversity

title: Joint Genome-Wide Profiling of miRNA and mRNA Expression in Alzheimer's Disease Cortex Reveals Altered miRNA Regulation

title: Roles of the Src Tyrosine Kinases Lck and Fyn in Regulating γδTCR Signal Strength

Yet, the critical mechanistic details of SNARE-catalyzed membrane fusion are poorly understood, especially during rapid synaptic transmission. Here, we systematica

Demographically-Inspired Query Variants Using an LLM Conference: Proceedings of the 2025 International ACM SIGIR Conference on Innovative Concepts and Theories in Information Retrieval (ICTIR); July 18, 2025; Padua, Italy Proceedings of the 2025 International ACM SIGIR Conference on Innovative Conce
creator: Marwah Alaofi, Nicola Ferro, Paul Thomas, Falk Scholer, Mark Sanderson
description: Abstract . This study proposes a method to diversify queries in existing test collections to reflect some of the diversity of search engine users, aligning with an earlier vision of an ‘ideal’ test collection. A LLM ( LLM ) is used to create query variants: alternative queries that have the same meaning as the original.

title: SEBVS : Synthetic Event-based Visual Servoing for Robot Navigation and Manipulation
creator: Krishna Vinod, Prithvi Jai Ramesh, Pavan Kumar B N, Bharatesh Chakravarthi
description: Abstract Event cameras offer microsecond latency, high dynamic range, and low power consumption, making them ideal for real-time robotic perception under challenging conditions such as motion blur, occlusion, and illumination changes. However, despite their advantages, synthetic event-based vision remains largely unexplored in mainstream robotics simulators.

title: Unlearning as Ablation: Toward a Falsifiable Benchmark for Generative Scientific Discovery
creator: Robert Yang
description: Abstract Bold claims about AI’s role in science—from “AGI will cure all diseases” to promises of radically accelerated discovery—raise a central epistemic question: do large language models (LLMs) truly generate new knowledge, or do they merely remix memorized fragments? We propose unlearning-as-ablation as a falsifiable probe of constructive scientific discovery.

title: RRAT J2325–0530: A Rotating Radio Transient with an Atypical Waiting-time Distribution Facilities: The Five-hundred-meter Aperture Spherical radio Telescope (FAST). Astropy ( Astropy Collaboration et al. 2013 ) , Bilby ( G. Ashton et al. 2019 ) , clfd ( V. Morello et al. 2019 ) , DSPSR ( W. van Stra
creator: Shi-Jie Gao, Xiang-Dong Li, Zhen Yan, Yi-Xuan Shao, Ping Zhou
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Shi-Jie Gao, Xiang-Dong Li, Zhen Yan, Yi-Xuan Shao, Ping Zhou. We present 1.25 GHz observations of the rotating radio transient (RRAT) J2325–0530, conducted with the Five-hundred-meter Aperture Spherical radio Telescope (FAST). Approximately 60% of detected single pulses occur in clusters of 2 to 5 consecutive bursts. Consequently, the waiting-time distribution between successive single pulses exhibits a pronounced excess at one rotation period, deviating from the exponential distribution expected for a Poisson process.

title: A Target Search for Fast Radio Bursts Associated with Two Fast Blue Optical Transients: AT2018cow and CSS161010 Facilities: Five-hundred-meter Aperture Spherical radio Telescope (FAST). FRB Fake (Author: Leon Houben, https://gitlab.com/houben.ljm/frb-faker ), DSPSR ( van Straten & Bailes 2011 ) , He
creator: Shi-Jie Gao, Xiang-Dong Li, Yi-Xuan Shao, Ping Zhou, Pei Wang, Yun-Wei Yu, Zhen Yan, Di Li
description: Abstract Fast blue optical transients (FBOTs) are luminous, rapidly evolving events with blue spectra, possibly powered by newborn magnetars and linked to fast radio bursts (FRBs). Given this potential connection, we conducted deep radio observations of two nearby FBOTs (AT2018cow and CSS161010) using the Five-hundred-meter Aperture Spherical radio Telescope (FAST), but detected no FRB-like signals.

title: SurveyGen: Quality-Aware Scientific Survey Generation with Large Language Models
creator: Tong Bao, Mir Tafseer Nayeem, Davood Rafiei, Chengzhi Zhang
description: Abstract Automatic survey generation has emerged as a key task in scientific document processing. While large language models (LLMs) have shown promise in generating survey texts, the lack of standardized evaluation datasets critically hampers rigorous assessment of their performance against human-written surveys.

title: Characterizing the Behavior of Training Mamba-based State Space Models on GPUs
creator: Trinayan Baruah 1 Kaustubh Shivdikar 1 Sara Prescott 2 David Kaeli 3
description: Abstract Mamba-based State Space Models (SSM) have emerged as a promising alternative to the ubiquitous transformers. Despite the expressive power of transformers, the quadratic complexity of computing attention is a major impediment to scaling performance as we increase the sequence length.

title: Testing the weak cosmic censorship conjecture via test particle-induced overcharging/overspinning of Kerr–Newman-modified gravity black hole
creator: Waqar Ahmad (waqar.ahmad@cust.edu.pk), Abdul Rehman Kashif (kashmology@gmail.com)
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Waqar Ahmad (waqar.ahmad@cust.edu.pk), Abdul Rehman Kashif (kashmology@gmail.com). We investigate the weak cosmic censorship conjecture (WCCC) violation through the absorption of a charged, rotating test particle by Kerr-Newman spacetime in modified gravity (KN-MOG). The result is sensitive to multiple factors, including the sign of the particle’s charge relative to that of the black hole, as well as the direction of rotation of the particle and the black hole.

title: A Taxonomy of Transcendence
creator: Natalie Abreu, Edwin Zhang, Eran Malach & Naomi Saphra
description: Abstract Although language models are trained to mimic humans, the resulting systems display capabilities beyond the scope of any one person. To understand this phenomenon, we use a controlled setting to identify properties of the training data that lead a model to transcend the performance of its data sources.

title: ClearMask : Noise-Free and Naturalness-Preserving Protection Against Voice Deepfake Attacks Conference: ACM Asia Conference on Computer and Communications Security; August 25–29, 2025; Hanoi, Vietnam ACM Asia Conference on Computer and Communications Security (ASIA CCS ’25), August 25–29, 2025, Hano
creator: Yuanda Wang, Bocheng Chen, Hanqing Guo, Guangjing Wang, Weikang Ding, Qiben Yan
description: Abstract . Voice deepfake attacks, which artificially impersonate human speech for malicious purposes, have emerged as a severe threat. Existing defenses typically inject noise into human speech to compromise voice encoders in speech synthesis models. However, these methods degrade audio quality and require prior knowledge of the attack approaches, limiting their effectiveness is diverse scenarios.

title: CoCoA : Co nfidence- and Co ntext-Aware A daptive Decoding for Resolving Knowledge Conflicts in Large Language Models
creator: Anant Khandelwal, Manish Gupta, Puneet Agrawal
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Anant Khandelwal, Manish Gupta, Puneet Agrawal. Faithful generation in large language models (LLMs) is challenged by knowledge conflicts between parametric memory and external context. Existing contrastive decoding methods tuned specifically to handle conflict often lack adaptability and can degrade performance in low conflict settings. We introduce CoCoA ( Co nfidence- and Co ntext-Aware A daptive Decoding), a novel token-level algorithm for principled conflict resolution and enhanced faithfulness.

title: Partitions into sums of two squares
creator: Jaime Palacios
description: Abstract . We use a variation of the Circle Method, along with the Saddle Point Method, to obtain an asymptotic formula for the number of partitions of a number n n into integers which are sums of two squares. Unlike previous work on partitions into restricted parts, we need to handle a Dirichlet series with a fractional singularity. 1.

title: I Can’t Join, But I Will Send My Agent: Stand-in Enhanced Asynchronous Meetings (SEAM) CCS: Human-centered computing Mixed / augmented reality
creator: Zhongyi Bai, Jens Emil Grønbæk, Andrew Irlitti, Jarrod Knibbe, Eduardo Velloso
description: Abstract . We propose and explore the user experience of SEAM—Stand-in Enhanced Asynchronous Meetings—virtual reality meetings in which embodied virtual agents represent absent users. During the meeting, attendees can address the agent, and the absent user can later watch the recording from its perspective to respond.

We compare C 2 ​ ( ω ) C^{2}(\omega) to the previously studied inner model C ⁡ ( aa ) C(\hskip-1.0pt\mathop{{\mbox{\tt a\hskip-0.4pta}}}\hskip-1.0pt) .

title: An analogue of the Erdős Matching Conjecture for permutations with fixed number of cycles
creator: Cheng Yeaw Ku, Kok Bin Wong
description: Abstract Let S n S_{n} denotes the set of permutations of [ n ] = { 1 , 2 , … , n } [n]=\{1,2,\dots,n\} . For each integer k ≥ 1 k\geq 1 , let S n , k S_{n,k} be the set of all permutations of [ n ] [n] with exactly k k disjoint cycles.

title: Water structuring at stacked graphene interfaces unveiled by machine-learning molecular dynamics
creator: Dianwei Hou, Yevhen Horbatenko, Stefan Ringe, Minhaeng Cho
description: Abstract The wettability of monolayer and multilayer graphene remains a topic of longstanding debate. Here, we combined first-principles molecular dynamics simulations accelerated with the atomic cluster expansion machine learning interatomic potential to investigate how substrate, graphene layer number, and intercalated water molecules influence graphene’s wettability.

title: Strong averaging principle for nonautonomous multi-scale SPDEs with fully local monotone and almost periodic coefficients
creator: Mengyu Cheng, Xiaobin Sun, Yingchao Xie
description: Abstract . In this paper, we consider a class of nonautonomous multi-scale stochastic partial differential equations with fully local monotone coefficients. By introducing the evolution system of measures for time-inhomogeneous Markov semigroups, we study the averaging principle for such kind of system.

title: Language-Guided Temporal Token Pruning for Efficient VideoLLM Processing
creator: Yogesh Kumar
description: Abstract Vision Language Models (VLMs) struggle with long-form videos due to the quadratic complexity of attention mechanisms. We propose Language-Guided Temporal Token Pruning (LGTTP), which leverages temporal cues from queries to adaptively prune video tokens, preserving contextual continuity while reducing computational overhead. Unlike uniform pruning or keyframe selection, LGTTP retains higher token density in temporally relevant segments.

title: A convergence framework for energy minimisation of linear self-adjoint elliptic PDEs in nonlinear approximation spaces Thanks: ∗ Corresponding author
creator: Alexandre Magueresse †∗, Santiago Badia †
description: Abstract . Recent years have seen the emergence of nonlinear methods for solving partial differential equations (PDEs), such as physics-informed neural networks (PINNs). While these approaches often perform well in practice, their theoretical analysis remains limited, especially regarding convergence guarantees.

title: A Unsupervised Framework for Identifying Diverse Quantum Phase Transitions Using Classical Shadow Tomography
creator: Chi-Ting Ho, Daw-Wei Wang
description: Abstract We provide a general machine learning methodology that integrates classical shadow representations with unsupervised principal component analysis (PCA) to explore various quantum phase transitions. By sampling spin configurations from random Pauli measurements, our approach can effectively analyze hidden statistical patterns in the data, thereby capturing the distinct signatures of quantum criticality through their fluctuations.

title: Semantic Search for Information Retrieval
creator: Kayla Farivar
description: Abstract Information retrieval systems have progressed notably from lexical techniques such as BM25 and TF-IDF to modern semantic retrievers. This survey provides a brief overview of the BM25 baseline, then discusses the architecture of modern state-of-the-art semantic retrievers. Advancing from BERT, we introduce dense bi-encoders (DPR), late-interaction models (ColBERT), and neural sparse retrieval (SPLADE).

title: Database Normalization via Dual-LLM Self-Refinement CCS: Information systems Relational database model CCS: Computing methodologies Reasoning about belief and knowledge
creator: Eunjae Jo, Nakyung Lee, and Gyuyeong Kim
description: Abstract . Database normalization is crucial to preserving data integrity. However, it is time-consuming and error-prone, as it is typically performed manually by data engineers. To this end, we present Miffie, a database normalization framework that leverages the capability of large language models. Miffie enables automated data normalization without human effort while preserving high accuracy.

title: Copyright Protection for 3D Molecular Structures with Watermarking
creator: Runwen Hu, Peilin Chen, Keyan Ding, Shiqi Wang
description: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) revolutionizes molecule generation in bioengineering and biological research, significantly accelerating discovery processes. However, this advancement introduces critical concerns regarding intellectual property protection. To address these challenges, we propose the first robust watermarking method designed for molecules, which utilizes atom-level features to preserve molecular integrity and invariant features to ensure robustness against affine transformations.

title: Symbol Detection Using an Integrate-and-Fire Time Encoding Receiver Thanks: The author acknowledges the Office of the Chancellor of the University of the Philippines Diliman, through the Office of the Vice Chancellor for Research and Development, for funding support through the PhD Incentive Award G
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by . Event-driven sampling is a promising alternative to uniform sampling methods, particularly for systems constrained by power and hardware cost. A notable example of this sampling approach is the integrate-and-fire time encoding machine (IF-TEM), which encodes an analog signal into a sequence of time stamps by generating an event each time the integral of the input signal reaches a fixed threshold.

title: Adhesion Control through Electric Field-Induced Water Adsorption at Oxidized Silicon Interfaces
creator: H. Tunç Çiftçi, Jonathon Cottom, Rachid Hahury, Emilia Olsson, Bart Weber
description: Abstract Adhesion plays a pivotal role in computer chip manufacturing, directly affecting the precision and durability of positioning components such as wafer stages. Electrical biasing is widely employed to eliminate floating potential and to enable electrostatic clamping. However, upon electrical grounding adhesion can persist and there is limited knowledge about the nature of this adhesion hysteresis.

title: NGD: Neural Gradient Based Deformation for Monocular Garment Reconstruction
creator: Soham Dasgupta, Shanthika Naik, Preet Savalia, Sujay Kumar Ingle, Avinash Sharma
description: Abstract Dynamic garment reconstruction from monocular video is an important yet challenging task due to the complex dynamics and unconstrained nature of the garments. Recent advancements in neural rendering have enabled high-quality geometric reconstruction with image/video supervision. However, implicit representation methods that use volume rendering often provide smooth geometry and fail to model high-frequency details.

title: Indefinite structure of the Bergman kernel on the open unit disk
creator: Kenta KOJIN
description: Abstract In this paper, we focus on an indefinite structure lying behind the Bergman kernel on the open unit disk. In particular, an invariant distance, birational maps and an indefinite kernel are constructed from the Bergman kernel, and we deal with their interaction.

title: Deception in Asymmetric Information Homicidal Chauffeur Game
creator: Shreesh Mahapatra, Bhargav Jha, Michael R. Dorothy, Shaunak D. Bopardikar
description: Abstract The classic Homicidal Chauffeur game is a pursuit-evasion game played in an unbounded planar environment between a pursuer constrained to move with fixed speed on curves with bounded curvature, and a slower evader with fixed speed but with simple kinematics.

title: Copas-Jackson-type bounds for publication bias over a general class of selection models
creator: Taojun Hu Department of Biomedical Statistics, Graduate School of Medicine, Osaka University, 565-0871, Osaka, Japan Department of Biostatistics, School of Public Health, Peking University, 100191, Beijing, China, Yi Zhou Beijing International Center for Mathematical Research, Peking University, 100
description: Abstract Publication bias (PB) is one of the most vital threats to the accuracy of meta-analysis. Adjustment or sensitivity analysis based on selection models, which describe the probability of a study being published, provide a more objective evaluation of PB than widely-used simple graphical methods such as the trim-and-fill method. Most existing methods rely on parametric selection models.

title: The Impact of Silicate Grain Coagulation on Millimeter Emission from Massive Protostellar Disks
creator: Ryota Yamamuro, Kei E. I. Tanaka, Satoshi Okuzumi
description: Abstract Hot accretion disks around massive protostars provide a unique opportunity to study ice‐free silicate grains that cannot be investigated in protoplanetary disks. We conduct a self‐consistent investigation into grain size evolution and its impact on (sub-)millimeter-wave emission from massive protostellar disks. Our radiative transfer modeling accounts for dust self-scattering and includes vertical temperature gradients in the disk structure.

title: How Machine Learning Predicts Fluid Densities under Nanoconfinement
creator: Yuanhao Li
description: Abstract Fluids under nanoscale confinement differ – and often dramatically – from their bulk counterparts. A notorious feature of nanoconfined fluids is their inhomogeneous density profile along the confining dimension, which plays a key role in many fluid structural and transport phenomena in nanopores.

title: Enhancing LLM-Based Social Bot via an Adversarial Learning Framework
creator: Fanqi Kong, Xiaoyuan Zhang, Xinyu Chen, Yaodong Yang, Song-Chun Zhu, Xue Feng
description: Abstract Developing Large Language Model (LLM) agents that exhibit human-like behavior, encompassing not only individual heterogeneity rooted in unique user profiles but also adaptive response to socially connected neighbors, is a significant research challenge. Social media platforms, with their diverse user data and explicit social structures, provide an ideal testbed for such investigations.

title: On the Edge of Memorization in Diffusion Models
creator: Sam BuchananTTIC, Druv PaiUC BerkeleyYi MaUC Berkeley, HKUValentin De BortoliGoogle DeepMind
description: Abstract When do diffusion models reproduce their training data, and when are they able to generate samples beyond it? A practically relevant theoretical understanding of this interplay between memorization and generalization may significantly impact real-world deployments of diffusion models with respect to issues such as copyright infringement and data privacy.

title: SMITE: Enhancing Fairness in LLMs through Optimal In-Context Example Selection via Dynamic Validation
creator: Garima Chhikara, Kripabandhu Ghosh, Abhijnan Chakraborty
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Garima Chhikara, Kripabandhu Ghosh, Abhijnan Chakraborty. Large Language Models (LLMs) are widely used for downstream tasks such as tabular classification, where ensuring fairness in their outputs is critical for inclusivity, equal representation, and responsible AI deployment. This study introduces a novel approach to enhancing LLM performance and fairness through the concept of a dynamic validation set, which evolves alongside the test set, replacing the traditional static validation approach.

title: Talking to Robots: A Practical Examination of Speech Foundation Models for HRI Applications
creator: Theresa Pekarek Rosin, Julia Gachot, Henri-Leon Kordt, Matthias Kerzel, Stefan Wermter
description: Abstract Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) systems in real-world settings need to handle imperfect audio, often degraded by hardware limitations or environmental noise, while accommodating diverse user groups. In human–robot interaction (HRI), these challenges intersect to create a uniquely challenging recognition environment.

title: Sustainability or Survivability? Eliminating the Need to Choose in LEO Satellite Constellations
creator: Chris Misa, Ramakrishnan Durairajan
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Chris Misa, Ramakrishnan Durairajan. LEO Satellite Networks (LSNs) are revolutionizing global connectivity, but their reliance on tens of thousands of satellites raises pressing concerns over sustainability and survivability. In this work, we argue that the inefficiencies in LSN designs stem from ignoring the strong spatiotemporal structure of Internet traffic demand (which impacts sustainability) and the physical realities of the near-Earth space environment (which affects survivability).

title: From Global to Local: Social Bias Transfer in CLIP
creator: Ryan Ramos, Yusuke Hirota, Yuta Nakashima, Noa Garcia
description: Abstract The recycling of contrastive language-image pre-trained (CLIP) models as backbones for a large number of downstream tasks calls for a thorough analysis of their transferability implications, especially their well-documented reproduction of social biases and human stereotypes. How do such biases, learned during pre-training, propagate to downstream applications like visual question answering or image captioning? Do they transfer at all?

title: Evaluating the Quality of the Quantified Uncertainty for (Re)Calibration of Data-Driven Regression Models
creator: Jelke Wibbeke, Nico Schönfisch, Sebastian Rohjans, Andreas Rauh
description: Abstract In safety-critical applications data-driven models must not only be accurate but also provide reliable uncertainty estimates. This property, commonly referred to as calibration, is essential for risk-aware decision-making. In regression a wide variety of calibration metrics and recalibration methods have emerged.

title: Towards Trustworthy Breast Tumor Segmentation in Ultrasound using Monte Carlo Dropout and Deep Ensembles for Epistemic Uncertainty Estimation
creator: Toufiq Musah, Chinasa Kalaiwo, Maimoona Akram, Ubaida Napari Abdulai, Maruf Adewole, Farouk Dako, Adaobi Chiazor Emegoakor, Udunna C. Anazodo, Prince Ebenezer Adjei, Confidence Raymond
description: Abstract Automated segmentation of BUS images is important for precise lesion delineation and tumor characterization, but is challenged by inherent artifacts and dataset inconsistencies. In this work, we evaluate the use of a modified Residual Encoder U-Net for breast ultrasound segmentation, with a focus on uncertainty quantification.

title: EEG-FM-Bench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for the Systematic Evaluation of EEG Foundation Models
creator: Wei Xiong, Jiangtong Li, Jie Li, Kun Zhu
description: Abstract Electroencephalography (EEG) foundation models are poised to significantly advance brain signal analysis by learning robust representations from large-scale, unlabeled datasets. However, their rapid proliferation has outpaced the development of standardized evaluation benchmarks, which complicates direct model comparisons and hinders systematic scientific progress. This fragmentation fosters scientific inefficiency and obscures genuine architectural advancements.

title: Puzzle : Scheduling Multiple Deep Learning Models on Mobile Device with Heterogeneous Processors Thanks: Qualcomm AI Research is an initiative of Qualcomm Technologies, Inc.
creator: Duseok Kang, Yunseong Lee, Junghoon Kim
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Duseok Kang, Yunseong Lee, Junghoon Kim. As deep learning models are increasingly deployed on mobile devices, modern mobile devices incorporate deep learning-specific accelerators to handle the growing computational demands, thus increasing their hardware heterogeneity. However, existing works on scheduling deep learning workloads across these processors have significant limitations: most studies focus on single-model scenarios rather than realistic multi-model scenarios, overlook performance variations from different hardware/software configurations, and struggle with accurate execution time estimation.

title: Magnetic reversals in a geodynamo model with a stably-stratified layer
creator: Nicolás P. Müller, Christophe Gissinger, François Pétrélis
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Nicolás P. Müller, Christophe Gissinger, François Pétrélis. We study the process of magnetic reversals in the presence of a stably-stratified layer below the core-mantle boundary using direct numerical simulations of the incompressible magnetohydrodynamics equations under the Boussinesq approximation in a spherical shell. We show that the dipolar-multipolar transition shifts to larger Rayleigh numbers in the presence of a stably-stratified layer, and that the dipolar strength of the magnetic field at the core-mantle boundary increases due to the skin effect.

title: The 5-step Solvable Mono-anabelian Reconstruction of Abelian Number Fields
creator: Yu Mao
description: Abstract In this paper, we develop a new method to reconstruct an abelian number field K K from the maximal 5 5 -step solvable quotient of G K G_{K} group-theoretically. The new aspect of this paper is that the results in this paper are independent from the bi-anabelian results proved in [ ST22 ] .

title: The Impact of Axion-Like Particles on Late Stellar Evolution
creator: I. Domínguez, O. Straniero, L. Piersanti, M. Giannotti, A. Mirizzi
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by I. Domínguez, O. Straniero, L. Piersanti, M. Giannotti, A. Mirizzi. Stars with masses ranging from 3 to 11 M ⊙ exhibit multiple evolutionary paths. Less massive stars in this range conclude their evolution as carbon-oxygen (CO) white dwarfs.

creator: Vladimir Rovenski
description: Abstract The recent interest of geometers in the f f -structures of K. Yano (1961) is motivated by the study of the dynamics of contact foliations, as well as their applications in theoretical physics. Weak metric f f -structures on a smooth manifold, introduced by of the author and R.

title: ISACL: Internal State Analyzer for Copyrighted Training Data Leakage
creator: Guangwei Zhang, Qisheng Su, Jiateng Liu, Cheng Qian, Yanzhou Pan, Yanjie Fu, Denghui Zhang
description: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) have revolutionized Natural Language Processing (NLP) but pose risks of inadvertently exposing copyrighted or proprietary data, especially when such data is used for training but not intended for distribution. Traditional methods address these leaks only after content is generated, which can lead to the exposure of sensitive information.

title: On the Smallest Singular Value of Log-Concave Random Matrices
creator: Galyna V. Livshyts, Manuel Fernandez V, Stephanie Mui
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Galyna V. Livshyts, Manuel Fernandez V, Stephanie Mui. Let A A be an N × n N\times n random matrix whose entries are coordinates of an isotropic log-concave random vector in ℝ N ​ n \mathbb{R}^{Nn} .

title: Revisiting Hötte 2025 : A Companion Analysis with Extended Evidence from UK Inter-Industry Payment Data, 2017–2024
creator: Kerstin Hötte
description: Abstract In 2025, the UK Office for National Statistics released a novel dataset of monthly inter-industry payment flows during January 2017 to November 2024 at the 5-digit SIC level ( ONS 2025 ) , covering > > 3.1 million UK organizations. Annual aggregates amount to 490 million transactions with an aggregate value of over £3.1 trillion in 2023.

title: Optimization of centroidal Voronoi tessellations Thanks: This work has been partially supported by the Brazilian agencies FAPESP (grants 2013/07375-0, 2022/05803-3, and 2023/08706-1) and CNPq (grant 302073/2022-1).
creator: Ernesto G. Birgin, Juan S. C. Franco, Antoine Laurain
description: Abstract In this paper, we investigate the optimization of Centroidal Voronoi Tessellations (CVT) under geometric constraints. For this purpose, we minimize a linear combination of the standard CVT energy functional with terms involving geometric attributes such as area and perimeter.

title: Energy minimisation using overlapping tensor-product free-knot B-splines Thanks: ∗ Corresponding author
creator: Alexandre Magueresse †∗, Santiago Badia †
description: Abstract . Accurately solving pde with localised features requires refined meshes that adapt to the solution. Traditional numerical methods, such as finite elements, are linear in nature and often ineffective for such problems, as the mesh is not tailored to the solution.

title: Mapping of Fermionic Lattice Models for Ising Solvers
creator: Lakshya Nagpal, Aditya Kumar, S. R. Hassan
description: Abstract We present an end-to-end, symmetry-aware pipeline that converts interacting fermionic and quantum-spin models into annealer-ready QUBOs while preserving low-energy physics. The workflow combines Bravyi–Kitaev encoding, exact ℤ 2 \mathbb{Z}_{2} symmetry tapering, Xia–Bian–Kais (XBK) diagonalization to a Z-only form, and k → 2 k\!\to\!2 quadratization, with ground energies recovered via a Dinkelbach fixed-point over the resulting Ising objective.
